anchor.quote: Let $d$ be the number of cyclic coordinates of an array, a positive integer.
The index $\ell$ names a coordinate, running from $1$ to $d$.
let $L_\ell$ be the cyclic length of coordinate $\ell$

gaps.quote: In the construction, one axis is given length $r$ and taken as the last one, so $L_d = r$:
gaps.note: The page never says which construction is meant, so the reader cannot check why one axis gets length r and becomes the last coordinate.

gaps.quote: The wrap-around of the last coordinate therefore reappears as a sign change in the polynomial ring.
gaps.note: The page gives no derivation of why wrapping modulo r turns into a sign change modulo y^r + 1; the reader must take it on trust from the phase twist page.
